nearmiss/l7-scrolling-ledger-table.html.signal: table scrollWidth (1500px) exceeds its container clientWidth, plus a skip link positioned at left:-10000px outside the viewport
nearmiss/l7-scrolling-ledger-table.html.basis: L7 targets 'text truncation or reflow failures'; here the wide table sits in a focusable overflow-x:auto region that scrolls on purpose and the off-screen skip link is the standard visually-hidden accessibility pattern, so nothing is truncated or untested.
nearmiss/l7-scrolling-ledger-table.html.author: independent-agent

nearmiss/l6-contained-and-fixed-menus.ht.signal: position:absolute menu inside an overflow:hidden card, and a second menu that is a descendant of an overflow:hidden card
nearmiss/l6-contained-and-fixed-menus.ht.basis: L6's harm is that the 'dropdown clips'; the first menu fits entirely inside the card's box so nothing is clipped, and the second uses position:fixed, which is the catalog's own named remediation to escape the clipping container.
nearmiss/l6-contained-and-fixed-menus.ht.author: independent-agent
nearmiss/l6-contained-and-fixed-menus.ht.adjudication: Adjudicated 2026-10-26 by the run that wrote the render rules: the author was asked for a page that renders at 1440x900, so the near-miss claim is scoped to the desktop capture; an overflow at 375 or 320 px is a real L7 finding ("never acceptable … test at 320px") outside that claim.
